You move to Dr. Ren's console, the proximity to her analytical rig feeling charged, almost hostile. The holographic projector flares into life above the interface, displaying a schematic so complex it defies immediate comprehension—a fractal blueprint of Node Three integrated directly into the station's structural manifold.

Ren doesn’t flinch at the complexity; she lives in this chaos. She manipulates the projections, isolating the patterns that define the Entity’s active defense matrix. Her fingers move across the control surface with desperate precision, navigating through layers of assimilation and counter-signal architecture.

"It doesn't just block," Ren explains, zooming in on a dense knot of data lines within Node Three’s structure. "It assimilates the *intent* of the disruption. When we hit it with an EM field, it instantly refines its matrix to absorb that frequency as part of its operational code."

The schematic shifts to model the proposed kinetic overload pulse (Helena's Option Three). Ren traces the projected energy flow through the integrated architecture. Her face drains of color; she knows what this data means for your options.

"We are fighting an optimization process," she says, looking at Node Three with a chilling mixture of fear and professional resolve.
